items.title: 4.3.4 Combining List and Stack to Perform Sequential Operations

source_refs.note: Topic 4.3.4 (PDF 121-122, printed 118-119). The reversal code is not from the book; flagged.

blocks.text: A list stores data flexibly and a stack imposes Last-In, First-Out order, so together they handle tasks where the most recent element must be processed first. To reverse [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]: push each element onto an empty stack, then pop them one by one back into the list. Because the stack is LIFO, the list becomes [50, 40, 30, 20, 10].

blocks.title: Python code (each .... is one 4-space indent)
blocks.text:
numbers = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]
stack = []
for n in numbers:
....stack.append(n)          # push
numbers = []
while stack:
....numbers.append(stack.pop())    # pop back into the list
print(numbers)    # [50, 40, 30, 20, 10]

blocks.prompt: Name two other tasks where a list and a stack work together.
blocks.explanation: Undo (a list of document states with a stack of recent actions) and backtracking (a list of choices with a stack of the path tried so far).

items: List plus stack: push all, pop all, and the order is reversed: [50, 40, 30, 20, 10].
